OUR NAME,
OUR POINT OF VIEW.

We start by
looking closer.

RIKU stands for Research in Imaging, Knowledge & Understanding. We begin with computer vision, then bring different perspectives together to explore questions that cross disciplines.

05 / PUBLICATIONS2026 / THREE PAPERS ✳
OUR RESEARCH, IN PRINT

Ideas worth
sharing.

Three views into MRI-based prediction of perineural invasion, from anatomy-guided learning to efficient routing and ordered slices.

RIKU team members are underlined in blue.

01 ✳
AICAS 2026 · ACCEPTEDARXIV:2607.11987

Anatomy-Privileged Distillation with Token Routing for MRI-Based Prediction of Perineural Invasion

Hyunsu Go, Youngung Han, Kyeonghun Kim, Junga Kim, Dohyun Kweon, Jinyong Jun, Sungha Park, Anna Jung, Induk Um, Yului Jeong, Suah Park, Jina Jeong, Pa Hong, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Won Jae Lee, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

An anatomy-guided teacher helps an MRI-only student learn to predict perineural invasion without masks at inference.

READ PAPER ↗
02 ✦
AICAS 2026 · ACCEPTEDARXIV:2607.11533

Adaptive Routing for Efficient Diffusion Transformer-Based PNI Prediction

Youngung Han, Dohyun Kweon, Kyeonghun Kim, Hyunsu Go, Jina Jeong, Suah Park, Induk Um, Junga Kim, Anna Jung, Yului Jeong, Sungha Park, Jinyong Jun, Pa Hong, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Won Jae Lee, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

Adaptive routing across attention, spatial tokens, and MLP width makes diffusion Transformer-based MRI prediction more efficient.

READ PAPER ↗
03 ♡
APCCAS 2026 · ACCEPTEDARXIV:2609.11271

Order-Aware 2.5D Multiple Instance Learning for Preoperative MRI-Based Perineural Invasion Risk Assessment in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma

Hyunsu Go, Youngung Han, Kyeonghun Kim, Jinyong Jun, Junbeom Lee, Dohyun Kweon, Yului Jeong, Suah Park, Sungha Park, Anna Jung, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

Ordered 2.5D MRI slabs and multiple instance learning support patient-level risk assessment from weak labels.

WHY RIKU?

A name with
a little wish.

Our name takes inspiration from Maeda Riku of NCT WISH. We carry some of that bright, playful energy into how we work: finding good questions and shaping answers together.

Our wish is to keep our perspective moving. When ideas from different fields meet, they can open possibilities none of us expected.
